
=================================================================
#67 Onjo  (-18)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Fall of Euija · place: michuhol · tone: founder fairy tale
Logline: Nobody in their father’s hall ever mentions Buyeo. Then a boy with a sling turns up.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Every child in Baekje can tell you this story. Most of them get the beginning wrong.
[1] ¶ Onjo and Biryu grow up princes in their father’s hall. Nobody there ever mentions Buyeo.
[2] [MAP -18: ]
[3] ── SCENE: Buyeo ──
[4] ¶ In Buyeo, **Lady Ye** has raised Jumong’s first son alone.
[5] ¶ **Yuri** is a boy with a sling and bad aim, or good aim and bad luck. The pebble cracks a woman’s water jar on her way back from the well.
[6] [CARD King Yuri: Yuri. Bad aim or bad luck, and a mother who will not answer one question.]
[7] Water-carrier: Whose son are you, anyway? No father, no manners.
[8] King Yuri: What kind of man was my father? Where is he now?
[9] Lady Ye: Your father was no ordinary man. The country couldn’t hold him. / He went south and made himself a king. / He left something under the pine on the seven-sided stone. / Find it, and he’ll know you.
[10] ¶ There is no pine on any hill he climbs. He finds it at home: the house’s pine pillar stands on a seven-sided foundation stone, and in the crack beneath it lies half a sword.
[11] Lady Ye: Yuri….!
[12] ¶ With his friends, three boys as stubborn as he is, he walks his father’s road backwards, south.
[13] ── SCENE: The Half Sword ──
[14] ¶ In the hall at Jolbon he lays the half-sword on the boards. Jumong goes to a chest nobody has opened since the river, takes out the other half, and kneels. The two halves click.
[15] King Yuri: Father…!
[16] ¶ Onjo and Biryu watch from the porch rail. The rail already knows what the hall will decide.
[17] ── SCENE: The Last Night ──
[18] ¶ When Yuri is named crown prince, Sosuno does not fight the hall. She packs her dusty-rose silk. She packs the boys. She leaves the well.
[19] ¶ Jumong finds her at the old well, two buckets that have outlived the argument. Twenty winters in the same yard. He is still grinning. She is still pretending she came for water.
[20] Jumong: Hey. / You’re packed. / That’s… a lot of buckets for one road.
[21] Sosuno: Not buckets. / Grain. Boys. Me.
[22] Jumong: I left iron under a pine. I didn’t think it would grow up and walk in—
[23] Sosuno: Don’t— don’t make a speech. I’ll hit you.
[24] Jumong: Wasn’t going to. / Well’s still here. / I kept it. For you. Stupid, I know.
[25] Sosuno: Don’t be nice. / I’ll get stupid. / Yuri can have the chair. I’m not sitting in a footnote. / You know that. You always knew.
[26] Jumong: Yeah. / South, then. / Take the glow. Leave me the well. / …Come here. Please. One night. I’m still thirsty.
[27] Sosuno: Big idiot. / The boys are asleep. / If you compliment me I will scream. / …That’s not a no.
[28] ¶ They do not make it to a feast. They make it to the grain room that has been theirs since the first night, and she kisses him before the door is shut.
[29] ¶ Older. Hungrier. The hide has been off for years and she is worse now, not better.
[30] Jumong: Still you. / Still that mouth. / Look at you. Older. Better. Sorry. Not sorry.
[31] Sosuno: Don’t— ha— don’t you dare be sweet now. / Twenty winters, and you still breathe like you ran here. / …Slower. No. Not slower. / I want to remember this one. I’m not getting another.
[32] Jumong: Then don’t count. / I’ll count. / You know I’m bad at it.
[33] Sosuno: I hate you. I hate you, don’t stop— / …Say it. The thing you never say. / Say it now, while I can’t hit you.
[34] ¶ He says it into her hair. Even the sky looks away for this part. She laughs, and then she doesn’t, and the lamp burns down to a coal.
[35] Jumong: There. / Now you have to come back someday and hit me for it.
[36] ¶ Before dawn the lamp is out, and neither of them has slept.
[37] Sosuno: Don’t be nice. / I’ll get stupid. / …I’m already stupid. / Keep the well. I’m taking the glow.
[38] Jumong: Take it. / You’re beautiful. / Go found the other one. I’ll be here. Grinning. Like an idiot.
[39] ── SCENE: The Road South ──
[40] ¶ At dawn ten men start packing carts before anyone tells them to. Onjo and Biryu take their mother south. She walks like a woman who has been thoroughly answered and will not explain it to a deer, a son, or a chronicle.
[41] ¶ Three days south of the river, on a ridge path too narrow for the cart, a stag is standing in the way. Pale as mulberry paper, gold wherever the light touches it, antlers branching like a winter tree somebody decided to keep. It does not run. It looks at the three of them as if it had been told to expect three.
[42] Biryu: Don’t move. / That’s dinner for ten ministers. The antlers alone, a month of—
[43] Onjo: Hyung. Hyung, wait. / …That look like dinner to you? Really?
[44] Biryu: Looks like antlers to me. Meat with antlers.
[45] Sosuno: Biryu. Lower it. / …Listen to your mother. Bow down.
[46] ¶ Biryu lowers the bow the way an elder son does, slowly enough that everyone understands it was his own idea. The stag turns, walks ten paces up the ridge, and stops to look back. When they do not follow, it waits. When they do, it walks on. It keeps that up for nine days.
[47] Onjo: It wants us to follow, right? / …A deer knows the way, Mother?
[48] Sosuno: Your father crossed a river on turtles’ backs. / A deer’s practically civilised.
[49] ── SCENE: Mount Buak ──
[50] ¶ On the ninth day it takes them up Mount Buak, and from the top the brothers see all of it: a river looped across the plain like a belt somebody has unbuckled, high peaks at their backs, wet green flats to the south and, somewhere past the haze, the sea. Biryu smells the salt before he sees it.
[51] Biryu: Smell that? Sea. I’m going there. / River in front, mountains behind, sure, lovely. You can’t float a ship on it.
[52] Onjo: Hyung, all ten of them say here. / …I mean, ten people can all be wrong, but all ten—
[53] Biryu: Then the ten can live here. / And Mother? Who’s Mother coming with?
[54] Sosuno: …Don’t ask me that.
[55] ¶ Nobody answers him. The stag, which has stood a little apart all morning, crosses the summit and lies down in the grass at Onjo’s feet, facing the river. Biryu laughs too loudly and says the deer has no taste, and takes his half of the people down to Michuhol and the salt flats. The stag stays. Baekje will call it **Sinrok**, the guardian deer, for as long as Baekje has anything to call.
[56] [PLACE michuhol: Salt flats and sea wind. Biryu calls it a view.]
[57] Onjo: The land of ten tribes… Sipje! Hey, c’mon… we can think bigger than that. The land of a HUNDRED tribes… Baekje! Now that’s more like it….
[58] Onjo: “Baekje” — how does that sound?
[59] ¶ Biryu takes the sea. Onjo takes the river. Up north, their half-brother Yuri keeps the chair, and his line keeps it after him.
[60] ¶ So that is the family joke Euija and Gesomun used to throw at each other over wine. Goguryeo and Baekje are one father’s sons. One got the hall. One got the road. Neither has forgiven the other since.
[61] ¶ Seven hundred years later, the road ends at a riverbank in Sabi. Onjo’s heir is wringing the White River out of his sleeves. He once said a country is a territory governed by a single story. This was the story. He is about to learn who else can tell it.
[62] ¶ **Back to Sabi. Two armies are on the road, the boat for Gyebek still hasn’t sailed, and the king wants to know why…!**
